subtitle: Lesson 19 · Sampling & Estimation

eyebrow: Pull yourself up by your bootstraps

steps.label: Resample
steps.sub: Draw n values from your sample

code:
boot_means = np.array([
  rng.choice(orders, len(orders),
             replace=True).mean()
  for _ in range(10_000)])
boot_means.std(ddof=1)   # 4.42
stats.sem(orders)        # 4.50
np.percentile(boot_means, [2.5, 97.5])
# [27.5  44.76]
caption: Illustrative: 40 skewed order values.

code:
idx = rng.integers(0, 40,
                   size=(10_000, 40))
meds = np.median(orders[idx], axis=1)
np.percentile(meds, [2.5, 97.5])
# [19.98  42.59]   median was 25.4
caption: Vectorized: all resamples in one array.

code:
res = stats.bootstrap(
    (orders,), np.median,
    n_resamples=9999,
    method="percentile",
    random_state=1)
res.confidence_interval
# low 19.98, high 42.59
caption: Default method is BCa; check current docs for argument names.
